gap: The Transfer Case (line 109) introduces a district policy 'banning any tool that uploads student-created media to an outside server,' which is squarely a FERPA/student-data-privacy issue, yet the section cites no statute. A graduate teacher-ed AI-ethics course that repeatedly invokes privacy/consent with minors should ground at least one such constraint in FERPA/COPPA.
proposed_change: Add a brief parenthetical/footnote in the Transfer Case tying the 'no upload to outside server' policy to the real privacy regime: FERPA governs disclosure of education records to third-party vendors (permitted without consent only under the narrow 'school official exception'), and the amended COPPA Rule (effective June 23, 2025; full compliance by April 22, 2026) adds obligations including biometric data and separate consent for third-party disclosure for under-13 users. This shows the policy is a real legal standard, not an arbitrary scenario rule.

sources.cite: U.S. Dept. of Education, Student Privacy Policy Office — Responsibilities of Third-Party Service Providers under FERPA
sources.finding: FERPA bars disclosure of PII from education records to third parties (including edtech vendors) without consent unless an exception applies; the 'school official exception' requires the vendor be under district control and not redisclose data. This makes 'no upload to an outside server' a real FERPA-grounded constraint, not arbitrary.

sources.cite: FTC, Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule — Final Amendments, Federal Register (April 22, 2025)
sources.finding: The amended COPPA Rule is effective June 23, 2025, with full compliance required by April 22, 2026; it expands 'personal information' to include biometric data (e.g., facial recognition) and requires separate parental consent for third-party disclosures — directly relevant to uploading student-created media for under-13 students. Confirms the proposed '2025 COPPA rule update' framing.
